m: Climb up to the *archway* on top of the hill and snip at the wind with your *scissors*: you are standing on the **ridge**.
Two *legs* stick out of an *open crate*, and two more just like them beside it: a **matching pair**.
A *splashing water* fight soaks everyone, so they all beg for a warm **fur coat** to dry off in.
Two deer with *antlers* stand on one *scaffold*, shoulder to shoulder, **side by side**.
Two *horns* poke up from the top of a tennis bag: the handles of your **racket**.
A *bent knife* whistles past, and the quick **dodger** ducks just in time.
Pin the paper with a *tethered arrow* and trace round it on the *workbench*: you have made a **stencil**.
Up on the *hillside* someone stands with a **pointing finger**, showing you that house over there.
Tie a *silk thread* round the handle of a *ladle* so you won't forget: a **promise knot**.
A giant swings his fist into the *mountain* and knocks a chunk off with one **punch**.
Even the *scruffy dog* sits up straight and raises a paw in a **salute** when the old man lifts his *cane*.
A little roof is held up on one long *nail*: a wooden **pavilion** in the park.
A long ribbon flies from the corner of a *square* flag: the flapping **streamer**.
A *right hand* takes a partner's *thumb* and the two spin across the floor as **dance partners**.
*Water drops* pour in until a *bowing man* has to bend under the rising **flood**.
Tap a glass with your *cane* and light bounces off it in a bright **sparkle**.
A *tree* grows through an *archway*, and its branch has a sharp **thorn** that catches your sleeve.
Under the temple *roof* the priests keep one sacred arrow on the altar: the **temple arrow**.
The *sun* shines through the crack in the *gate*: there is a **gap** between the doors.
Two kids pull a rope over a *bent knife* stuck in the ground: a fierce **tug of war**.
The *standing person* rings the *wind chime* and calls out to the one in front of them: **you**!
A *cloth cover* is thrown over every *cart* as the **army** rolls off to war.
*Trudging feet* come down the stairs, followed by *mirror feet*: two sets of **descending feet**.
A *cloth cover* is thrown over a *small table* piled high with junk: a room full of **clutter**.
On the *hillside* sits a *nodding head*: your kind **auntie**, agreeing with everything you say.
*Wheat* waves on every *hillside* as far as you can see: this whole land is one **country**.
A *right hand* reaches down and blesses the *soil*: only a **saint** could make it grow like that.
A *cave* with only a *workbench* inside and nothing on it: an **empty room**.
Two *spoons* lie back to back, turned away from the warm south: they point **north**.
Someone shouts "*exit*!" and the *kneeling man* shuffles backwards in a hasty **retreat**.
The diner pushes his plate away and has a *turned head*: a **finished meal**.
Your *mouth* sips, and you feel like you have *spread wings*: a strong cup of **coffee**.
The *horns* rest on top of a *drying rack* to keep the cloth perfectly **flat**.
One *follower* and another sit down on the *soil* together: a **sitting pair**.
The bride draws a **long veil** over her face to keep off the *sun*.
A *bent knife* trims the hair, a *yoke* of new clothes goes on the shoulders: a total **makeover**.
The *kicking foot* of every *visitor* wears down the grass into a **pathway**.
An *early bird* lands on a *little fortune stick* raised high on a hilltop: a shining **beacon**.
A huge *mouth* shouts so loud it shakes the *sky*: what a **loudmouth**, everyone covers their ears.
The *sweating man* pulls so hard on the *bow* that it becomes a **bent bow**.
A *standing knife* carves every rule into a *shell*: the town's **rulebook**.
Lay the log on the back of a *cart* and bring down the *axe*: a **chopping block**.
Each *king* holds a jade stone: put them together and you have **twin jades**.
The *mouth* of the **sage** speaks words that fly straight and true, like an *arrow*.
Rope the *sail* down to the *workbench* to make a strong **brace**.
A *tied sack* full of *shells* hangs from a big **price tag**: very costly.
The *torso* turns, the *thumb* pulls back the string: the **archer** shoots.
Wearing a tin helmet like *armour* and leaving a muddy *paw print* on the table: the cheeky **monkey**.
Under the *blanket* each child gets one *lid* of rice: **even shares**.
The *minister* sneaks down at night and hides the gold deep inside the royal **vault**.
A *mouth* above a *shell*: the **employee** talks to customers and earns money.
A tiny green *beard* pushes up out of the *mountain*: the **sprout tip**.
An *antique* cat sits by the window, stares up at the *moon* and twitches its long **whiskers**.
*Joined hands* squeeze nervously past a *cobra* coiled on the stones of a narrow **alley**.
With a *long stride* the porter carries a *shoulder pole* across the palace **courtyard**.
A tired *visitor* steps in from the rain under your *roof*: welcome, dear **guest**, come in and sit.
The red *sun* sinks slowly behind the branches of the *family tree*: it is **twilight**.
A *rice field* of food sits under the *moon* of your belly: your **stomach**.
A *right hand* scatters *soybean* seeds in the field: that is your farmer **uncle**.
Long *grass* hangs down from the branches like hair: a **weeping willow**.
One *right hand* passes a gift down to another hand below: a careful **handover**.
A *feeding hand* offers *grass* that looks just like spinach: a sneaky **lookalike**.
With a *long stride* and a *writing brush* to sketch the plans, the **builder** gets to work.
One *mouth* stacked on another *mouth*, like the bones of your **spine**.
The *tree* whose purple fruit tastes as sweet as *candy*: a juicy **plum** tree.
Point to *this spot*: a bird's **beak**, curved and hard as an *ox horn*.
*Grass* piled on top like a *fitted lid*: a roof of **thatch**.
A *lying man* naps where the *arrow landing* marks his home: a little **cottage**.
Toss *hay* on the fire and your *heart* pounds: a **racing heart**.
Swallow a *pill* to settle your tummy before the great *feast*: a whole **roast**.
Two *nodding heads*, one above the other: the taller one is your **elder brother**.
Water from the *well* drops into a *pit* and gurgles a little **song**.
Under the hot *sun* the thirsty animals crowd round the long wooden feeding **trough**.
The *left hand* swings from the *elbow* up to the shoulder: your **upper arm**.
The *kneeling man* lifts his chin to the stars in an **upward gaze**.
*Trudging feet* climb up inside the narrow brick **chimney** to sweep out the soot.
The *sun* plants a *seedling* in the night sky and it grows into a **star**.
A *grain stalk* tied up with a pink *ribbon* suddenly bursts into **blossom**.
A *woman* is dragged off by a *right hand* to work all day: a tired **drudge**.
A *comb* scratches notes while *splashing water* is measured: the ship's **logbook**.
A *claw* grabs the end of the line and pulls you out of the river: a **rescue rope**.
*Two men* stand under the *sun*: when one gets tired, the other is his **substitute**.
A *helping hand* swings an *axe* at the branch: crack, now you have a **snapped stick**.
Bend your *elbow*, fire the *arrow*, and it stops dead in the target: **full stop**.
A *cross* on top, a *bean* shape below: a tall standing **drum**.
Two *horns* sit on top of a *wine jug*: the feast of the tribal **chieftain**.
Under the bright *sun* the *twins* kneel down to watch a tiny six-legged **insect**.
*Water drops* gush out where the *crowbar* pried open the rock: a **mountain spring**.
The *watcher* in the garden spots red *grass* among the beans: **amaranth**.
The *child* is served first from the big *dish*, because he is the **firstborn** of the family.
The fisherman lets the *fishing net* fall and heads for the *exit*: a **dropped net**.
The *sun* and the *moon* hang in the sky together, both shining at once: **sun and moon**.
On a *split log* sits the *night guard*, waiting for orders from his **general**.
All the *goods* in the *tree* are birds' nests, and they fill the air with **birdsong**.
A *claw* reaches into the *tree* and plucks: the busy **fruit picker**.
One *front runner* chases another *front runner*: **two racers** neck and neck.
The **inspector** walks along the kitchen and bends over every *dish*, peering closely for dirt.
Plant a *cross* in the warm sand to mark the way **south**.
The *helping hand* drags the *podium* across the stage: a **pulling hand**.
Two *horns* of ripe grain sprout on the *sapling*: a field of **barley**.
A *strong arm* pushes the plough through the muddy *rice field*: the hard-working **man**.
Rolling around in the *grass*, barking out a famous *quotation*: the **scruffy dog** thinks he is clever.
Pressing on the *grass* with a *heavy weight*, the film **director** shouts "cut!"
The *husband* grabs the toast with two *horns* of metal: a pair of **tongs**.
Put an *archway* of cloth over *two planks* of hair: a little **cap**.
The **debt collector** pulls up your *seedling top* to find the *shell* money you owe.
Thread every *shell* through the *pierced frame* one by one and you get a long **string of coins**.
A face painted like a *rice field*, held up by *joined hands*: a **strange mask**.
Stand on the *podium* and the *early bird* pins on your shiny **badge**.
Walk past the *stop sign*, and then the *trailing foot* catches up: that is one **step**.
The *knife* slices a *bent cross* into the loaf of bread: one quick **cut** and it falls apart.
The blazing *sun* beats down on the town for weeks without rest: a terrible **heatwave**.
Green *grass* shoots up in neat rows across the *rice field*: the **young crop**.
Push a stick through one *bullseye* and then another *bullseye*: a **kebab**.
One *sun* rises above another *sun* in the morning sky: a **double sun**, twice as bright.
A *spoon* balanced on top of a *page* makes it tip: a **tilted head**.
A *bent knife* digs a hole shaped like a *mortar*: a **trap pit**.
A *right hand* holds up another *right hand* next to it: clap them, and you are using **both hands**.
The *pig snout* sniffs the ground, then the big wild **hog** charges.
Plant a *cross* of twigs among the tall *grass* and let it grow bushy: a little **shrubbery**.
